correctness.rationale: The exact binomial weights yield \(b_0=1+nt\), \(b_1=\binom n2t^2\), and \(b_2=\binom n3t^3+\binom n4t^4\) for \(n\ge3\), where \(t=p/(1-p)>0\). For \(n=3,4\), the first gap is the only constraint; at \(n=5\), the second gap factors as \(5t^6(5t^2+18t+20)>0\). At \(n=6\), the index-one and index-three constraints require disjoint odds intervals \([1/3,2/3]\) and \([20/21,\infty)\). For \(n\ge7\), the first-gap quadratic discriminant is strictly negative, since with \(m=n-7\ge0\) the controlling factor is \(5m^4+98m^3+661m^2+1672m+912>0\), while the leading coefficient is negative. Hence the all-size theorem follows. The standalone checker verifies the identities symbolically and checks 1,200 independent rational examples; these finite checks are not substituted for the infinite argument.

originality.rationale: The primary 2019 full preprint, including Section 4 and Appendix A, and the published 2023 Section 4 discuss exactly the \(\lfloor2X/3\rfloor\) object, but give root/transport and strong-Rayleigh results rather than the sharp ordinary-log-concavity classification. Negative real-rootedness does not imply an ordinary-log-concavity failure. Further database and literature searches by object, grouped-coefficient alias, exact cutoffs and radicals gave no equivalent complete theorem; related archived statements concern different roundings or different shape questions. This establishes originality to the best of inspected public evidence, with the 2023 supplement and unindexed equivalents explicitly recorded as risks.
residual_risks: The separately published supplement DOI 10.1214/22-STS852SUPP was not accessible separately, although the longer 2019 preprint appendix was inspected; an uninspected additional argument is possible.

value.rationale: The law \(\lfloor2X/3\rfloor\) is a canonical rational quantization motivating a published research direction. Ordinary log-concavity is a substantive intermediate shape property not decided by previous real-rootedness obstructions. A complete classification with sharp algebraic parameter windows at \(n=3,4,5\) and the universal extinction of log-concavity from \(n=6\) onward is structurally informative; it is an all-sample-size result, not an arbitrary isolated numerical calculation. It separates admissible shape regimes from universal failure and informs shape-based approximations of rationally scaled binomial variables.
